\[
\mathbf{I}^{t+1} = \mathbf{I}^{t} + \lambda \sum_{n \in \{N,S,E,W\}} g\bigl(\lVert \nabla_n \mathbf{I}^{t} \rVert\bigr)\, \nabla_n \mathbf{I}^{t}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\mathbf{I}\): The color vector of a pixel
- \(\lVert \nabla_n \mathbf{I} \rVert\): The length of the color difference to neighbor n
- \(g\): The conduction function
- \(\lambda\): The step size

Bold I is the color vector (R, G, B). nabla_n is the color difference to the neighbor in direction n. Its length is the Euclidean distance between the two colors. All channels share the conduction g of that length, as Sapiro and Ringach propose for multivalued images.
